name: Bird Dog
summary: A quadruped core-stability exercise where opposite arm and leg are extended simultaneously while maintaining a neutral, stable spine.

aliases.text: Quadruped Opposite Arm and Leg Raise

setup: Assume a tabletop position on all fours with wrists stacked directly beneath shoulders and knees stacked beneath hips.
Align the spine in a neutral position with the neck neutral and gaze directed at the floor.
steps: Brace the midsection firmly to prevent the pelvis or ribcage from shifting.
Simultaneously reach one arm straight forward and extend the opposite leg straight back until both are parallel to the floor.
Pause for one to two seconds at the top, focusing on glute contraction and total spinal stability.
Smoothly return the hand and knee to the floor with control.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side or complete all reps on one side before switching.
instructions.breathing: Exhale smoothly as you reach outward, and inhale as you return to the quadruped starting position.
cues: Balance a glass of water on your lower back

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lower back as the leg lifts.
common_faults.correction: Lift the leg only to hip height and actively brace your abdominal wall to keep the lumbar spine flat.

common_faults.fault: Rotating the hips open toward the lifting side.
common_faults.correction: Keep your pelvis square to the floor by pointing the toes of the rear foot straight down.
Keep your chin slightly tucked and gaze directed between your hands to maintain a neutral cervical spine.

precautions: Use an exercise mat under the knees if you experience patellar discomfort.
